commit.message:
fix(create-wdio): make pnpm create wdio work with pnpm 11+, and test npm, pnpm, Yarn and Bun in CI (#16442)

* test(create-wdio): run the create-wdio e2e with npm, pnpm, Yarn or Bun

* test(create-wdio): check the create-wdio that @wdio/cli loads, also with pnpm

* fix(create-wdio): skip the pnpm build scripts so that pnpm create wdio works with pnpm 11 and later

* fix(create-wdio): install the packages that the generated tests import, for pnpm

* fix(create-wdio): show the install errors that Yarn writes to stdout

* ci(create-wdio): run the create-wdio e2e with npm, pnpm, Yarn and Bun

* docs(create-wdio): document the supported package managers and Yarn Plug'n'Play

* fix(create-wdio): save the pnpm build setting only for pnpm 11 and later, and tell what a parent workspace needs

* fix(create-wdio): review fixes for the pnpm workspace cases, the tests and the docs

- Use the project's own pnpm-workspace.yaml before a parent one (pnpm uses
  the nearest file).
- Inside a parent workspace, tell both cases: the parent file when it lists
  the project, else the project's own file. The starter and the wizard both
  explain it, so the message also shows when the install is skipped.
- Name the changed file in the message.
- Tests: matchers instead of mock.calls, realistic user agents, one helper
  for the parent workspace; e2e: literal types for the setups and the
  package managers.
- Docs: the pnpm note under pnpm, the Yarn note before its command, a Bun
  note.

* fix(create-wdio): do not break a flow-style pnpm-workspace.yaml, and find a quoted strictDepBuilds key

A line added after a flow mapping ({packages: [...]}) made the file invalid
(ERR_PNPM_INVALID_SETTING for every pnpm command). The wizard now leaves such
a file unchanged, passes the flag for its install and tells where to add the
setting. A quoted or flow-style strictDepBuilds key of the user is kept.

commit.message:
fix(session): import $$ in exported specs (#16441)

* fix(session): import $$ in exported specs

* fix(session): preserve selector references in exports

* fix(session): import $$ only for a bare reference and alias it only for a real assignment

- skip member names and object keys named $$ (browser.$$, el.$$, { $$: 1 })
- count only assignment targets: el.$$ = x, (await $$(s))[0].x = 1 and for (const $$ of …) keep the plain import
- text fallback: skip .$$ and arrow parameters, count compound and prefix updates
- read the hoisted import names from splitImports, compute the alias only when needed
- tests: one spec runner with a replacer function, so the alias gets $$ and not $
- e2e: drop the local Chrome binary, no-sandbox and junction options (not this topic)

* test(session): run the exported spec in strict mode, as an ES module runs

* fix(session): wrap the steps in a block only when a step declares its own $$

- a step that only assigns $$ keeps the steps flat, with the var copy first
- writes() replaces the name list, one marker check in the step renderer

* fix(session): end the $$ copy with a semicolon, use the block in the text fallback

- a first step that starts with ( or [ no longer continues the var $$ line
- the text fallback cannot see every declaration form, so it always uses the block
- the export parses steps with the same options as the exec parser

* fix(session): tighten the $$ text fallback and skip steps without $$

- the fallback finds a spread ...$$, and a postfix update on the line before $$ is not an assignment
- assignmentTarget() replaces the nested ternary
- the export parses without node locations, and without page objects skips steps with no $$
- tests: the fallback has its own cases; the annotation test has a correct name

* fix(session): keep a recorded function $$ when a step also assigns $$

A top-level function $$ hoists above the var $$ copy, which then overwrote it. The steps now go into the block, where the function is block-scoped.

---------

Co-authored-by: dprevost-perso-macos <plum117@hotmail.com>
